paragraphs.text: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)

Most people resist the idea of a true self-estimate, probably because they fear it might mean downgrading some of their beliefs about who they are and what they’re capable of. As Goethe’s maxim goes, it is a great failing “to see yourself as more than you are.” How could you really be considered self-aware if you refuse to consider your weaknesses? Don’t fear self-assessment because you’re worried you might have to admit some things about yourself. The second half of Goethe’s maxim is important too. He states that it is equally damaging to “value yourself at less than your true worth.” We underestimate our capabilities just as much and just as dangerously as we overestimate other abilities. Cultivate the ability to judge yourself accurately and honestly. Look inward to discern what you’re capable of and what it will take to unlock that potential.
① joy of uncovering and realizing hidden potential
② risk of judging others using subjective standards
③ necessity of evaluating oneself with precision and honesty
④ value of a precise analysis of the root cause to resolve the issue
⑤ benefits of focusing on own growth rather than comparing to others
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? (0.8점)

Too many times people, especially in today’s generation, expect things to just happen ⓐovernight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to ⓑdiscourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and ⓒcomplexity. If it doesn’t happen fast enough, we’re tempted to ⓓlose interest. So many people don’t want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. Have you ⓔfallen prey to impatience?
① ⓐ      ② ⓑ      ③ ⓒ      ④ ⓓ      ⑤ ⓔ
다음 단어의 영영풀이로 적절하지 않은 것은? (0.7점)
① phenomenon : something that happens or exists, especially something unusual
② prominent : not easily noticed by others and not well-known at all
③ obstinate : refusing to change one’s opinion or behavior despite good reasons
④ therapy : treatment intended to heal or to solve a problem over time
⑤ identification : proof of who you are, such as a card with your name and photo
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은? (0.8점)
① Students should learn to prioritize their tasks before exams.
② The twins looked so identical that even their parents were confused.
③ The eminent danger of flooding forced the village to evacuate.
④ The machine can detect tiny traces of chemicals in the air.
⑤ Children need to socialize with others to develop communication skills.
다음 주어진 해석에 대한 영작에서 밑줄 친 부분이 적절하지 않은 것은? (0.8점)
① 그녀는 의학 분야에서 경력을 추구하기로 결심했다.
→ She decided to pursue a career in medicine.
② 선약이 있어서 회의에 참석할 수 없었다.
→ I had a previous engagement, so I couldn’t attend the meeting.
③ 그 문서들은 기밀로 표시되어 공개 접근이 제한되었다.
→ The documents were marked as classified and restricted from public access.
④ 건강한 사회는 구성원 간의 신뢰에 달려 있다.
→ A healthy society depends on trust between its members.
⑤ 음악을 듣는 것은 스트레스를 받는 사람들에게 치유 효과가 있을 수 있다.
→ Listening to music can be therapeutic for people under stress.
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.9점)

To determine the mass of my bowling ball, I might put it onto a balance and compare it with a known mass, such as a number of metal cubes each weighing 1, 10, or 100 grams. Things get much more complicated if I want to know the mass of a distant star. How do I measure it? We can roughly say that measuring the mass of a star involves various theories. If we want to measure the mass of a binary star, we first determine a center of mass between the two stars, then their distance from that center which we can then use, together with a value for the period and a certain instance of Kepler’s Third Law, to calculate the mass. In other words, in order to “measure” the star mass, we measure other quantities and use those values, together with certain equations, to calculate the mass. Measurement is not a simple and unmediated estimation of independently existing properties, but ____________________________________________.
① a complex process determined by the observer’s effort
② an activity requiring chronological scientific knowledge
③ an act of freely using unverified formulas to determine units
④ a process for obtaining the result through various experiments
⑤ an assessment of values within prevailing theoretical frameworks
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)

Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn’t worry isn’t going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don’t even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
① Why Worrying Doesn’t Help?
② Letting Kids Take Control of Their Own Worry
③ The Difficulty of Separating Worry from Reality
④ How to Help Kids Express Their Negative Emotions
⑤ Understanding Children’s Emotions: How to Foster Emotional Intelligence
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? (1점)

To be mathematically literate means to be able to think critically about societal issues ⓐon which mathematics has bearing so as to make informed decisions about how to solve these problems. Dealing with such complex problems through interdisciplinary approaches, mirroring real-world problems ⓑrequire innovative ways of planning and organizing mathematical teaching methods. Navigating our world means being able to quantify, measure, estimate, classify, compare, find patterns, conjecture, justify, prove, and generalize within critical thinking and ⓒwhen using critical thinking. Therefore, making decisions, even ⓓqualitatively, is not possible without using mathematics and critical thinking. Thus, teaching mathematics should be done in interaction with critical thinking along with a decision-making process. They can be developed into the mathematical context, ⓔso that there is no excuse to not explicitly support students to develop them.
① ⓐ      ② ⓑ      ③ ⓒ      ④ ⓓ      ⑤ ⓔ
윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.9점)
① Similarly		Thus
② Likewise		However
③ For example	In contrast
④ Nevertheless	In short
⑤ On the contrary	In addition
다음 중 윗글에서 제시된 원인과 그 결과의 연결로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.9점)
① Smartphone diffusion → the standardization of information acquisition across all generations
② Shared formative social experiences → the formation of differences between generations
③ Increased individual choice → the disappearance of the concept of generations
④ Economic growth → the intensification of generational conflict
⑤ Social isolation → the development of digital technology
다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)

Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they’re able to buy. Look instead at what they’re forced to trade in return – look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don’t like. It will require – inevitably – realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well – but they haven’t truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, “Slavery resides under marble and gold.” Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you’re working hard toward? Let’s hope not.
① Only poor people lack freedom; the wealthy are always free.
② Fame and fortune guarantee ultimate happiness and freedom.
③ The cost of success is always worth it for the rich and famous.
④ Many successful people sacrifice their freedom for wealth and status.
⑤ True success means having wealth and power regardless of personal sacrifice.
다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)

Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action. You’d be pleased to receive the gift.

You’d say ‘thank you’, and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone’s character, we use words for various virtues: ‘generous’, ‘kind’, ‘courageous’, etc. A person who gives one gift isn’t generous. Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person’s ‘moral identity’, an emotional habit that is part of who you are. Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. Instant virtue is therefore impossible. Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
① True virtues are stable character traits formed over time.
② Generosity can be learned instantly through external tools.
③ Generosity is about doing something nice only when it is easy.
④ Generosity is about momentary actions, not a long-term trait.
⑤ Virtues are the result of random impulses rather than personal history.
[10~11] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

The cohort effect and the traditional notion of a generation are closely related. Broadly speaking, each generation is defined by the birth years of its members. According to the theory of generational cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular generation are socialized in distinct conditions compared to other generations. They experience similar political, economic, and social events during their early stages of life, which shape their beliefs, values, and behaviors in similar ways.

The cohort effect results in characteristic differences between generations. ______(A)______, Koreans went through the 1997 financial crisis, also known as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) crisis. Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time, and thus experienced great employment instability. This may have led them to prioritize secure employment for their children. ______(B)______, Gen Zers grew up with smartphones, and this earned them the “digital natives” label. They are accustomed to getting their news, information, and advice from social media. Their strength in using digital media, however, often leads them to lack social skills.
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? (1점)
These tactics have the potential to reorient us in profound ways, transforming our perspectives on our wait times.

“Tactics” is a term drawn from military usage. (A) Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. (B) In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by its own finite nature and the fact that we’re going to live only so long. (C) In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting. These aren’t tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. (D) Such renewed perspectives transform waiting from a burden to a springboard toward things like creativity, social critique, or reflection on our inner state and the state of our relationships. (E)
① (A)     ② (B)     ③ (C)     ④ (D)     ⑤ (E)
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? (1점)
Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life.

(A) For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month.

(B) Commitments make individuals’ behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform.

(C) Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the corresponding obligations가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.9점)

Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time thinking about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about the corresponding obligations that fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment’s thought to what they owe their friends is, to put it mildly, not a very good friend. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed to take the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and fans who never think about how they can be better fans even as they confidently opine about what athletes owe them are hardly fulfilling their end of the bargain.
① the expectations fans have about how athletes should behave
② the rewards fans get from watching their favorite athletes’ play
③ the emotional connections fans share with their favorite athletes
④ the pressures athletes feel to improve their performance for fans
⑤ the responsibilities that fans have in return for what they expect from athletes
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? (1점)
To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem.

The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. (A) The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. (B) He removes unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps sprays insecticides and fences off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. (C) Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. (D) If the grower stops intervening. even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. (E) Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
① (A)     ② (B)     ③ (C)     ④ (D)     ⑤ (E)
③ It reflected the experience of becoming adults with the beginning of the new millennium.
④ It was temporarily assigned due to an unclear birth-year range.
⑤ It was named to emphasize a generation’s adaptation to technological change.
윗글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)
① to criticize the causes of generational conflict
② to evaluate the lifestyle of a specific generation
③ to explain how generations are classified and named
④ to present solutions to problems of generational division
⑤ to emphasize value differences between generations
[20-21] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

ELIZA, the first chatbot, was designed by Joseph Weizenbaum, a professor at MIT’s artificial intelligence laboratory between 1964 and 1967. It was programmed to communicate with users, _____(A)______. When users typed questions and answers in the input box on the screen, ELIZA would give pre-programmed replies using a pattern-matching technique.

Weizenbaum claimed that ELIZA did not genuinely understand human language and that it was only programmed to follow pre-scripted patterns. However, users’ reactions to the program were quite surprising. The users felt like they were talking to someone who understood their input. They shared their worries and thoughts about their lives with ELIZA as if they were talking to a real psychotherapist.
윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (1점)
① playing the role of a psychotherapist
② analyzing users’ emotions in real time
③ generating responses through complex reasoning
④ interpreting the meaning of human language
⑤ evaluating users’ psychological conditions
윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)
① The Development of Early Artificial Intelligence at MIT
② The Role of Computers in Modern Psychotherapy
③ The Comparison of Language Abilities Between Humans and Machines
④ The Illusion of Understanding Created by Scripted Patterns
⑤ The Process of Emotional Analysis in Computer Programs
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (1점)

Mirror neurons form the neurological basis of empathy, making it important to investigate which animals possess these cells. So far, research has confirmed their presence in apes, but further studies across a wider range of species are needed to understand the full extent of their distribution. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They hypothesize that ______________________________________ are likely to have similar neural mechanisms. This idea is based on the fact that effective social interaction requires individuals to understand events from the perspective of others and to share, at least to some degree, their emotions. Even small creatures like goldfish might show early forms of this ability. As an animal that travels around in a tightly-knit group, it’s on board with this idea — or at least swimming alongside the boat.
① predatory animals hunting alone
② long-distance travelers following environmental cues
③ animals inhabiting herds or complex social structures
④ creatures living in random, unstructured environments
⑤ species with rigid dominance hierarchies preventing empathy
[18-19] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Sociologists classify generations based on an individual’s birth year. The four most recent generations are baby boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (or millennials), and Generation Z. Baby boomers are named so because the birth rate was significantly higher when they were born. But since Korea and the U.S. experienced dramatic population increases during different periods, their classifications of baby boomers differ accordingly. In the U.S., baby boomers are people born between 1946 and 1964, but in Korea, baby boomers are those born between 1955 and 1963. Generation X (1965-1980) earned its name from the title of a book written by Douglas Coupland in 1991. According to the book, people in their twenties in that era had a relaxed and laid-back lifestyle. The following generations, born after Generation X, were later called Y (1981-1996) and Z (1997-2012). Members of Generation Y are also called millennials because they became adults with the beginning of the new millennium.
다음 중 Generation X라는 명칭이 형성된 배경에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은? (0.8점)
① It reflected a social phenomenon of a sharp increase in the birth rate.
② It described the lifestyle of a specific age group through a book.
③ It reflected the experience of becoming adults with the beginning of the new millennium.
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸(A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

Do Gen Xers only care about job stability while Gen Zers are entirely selfish? Such simple classifications as this rarely prove to be accurate. The life cycle effect suggests that major life events, such as leaving home, separating from parents, getting married, or having children, can alter people’s values and attitudes. Many individuals say they used to be more adventurous and drawn to liberal lifestyles during their youth. But they tend to become more responsible after getting married and take fewer risks after having children.

A case in point is the assessment of millennials in the workplace. In the early 2000s, when this group initially entered the job market, they were perceived as being less committed to their companies. However, as they aged and got used to their roles, they began to be increasingly recognized as diligent workers. This illustrates that the pursuit of freedom is more characteristic of youth than of a specific generation, as certain attitudes and behaviors naturally develop during different life stages.
People’s values and attitudes change mainly with ___(A)___ rather than with ___(B￼)___, as responsibilities and priorities shift over time.
ㅣ 요  약  문 ㅣ
[22-23] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.

Suppose that you find information about something on the internet. Among the many search results, which link will you click? ⓐ Probably, the most attractive and eye-catching one. However , the information you have just found may not be valid even though it looks like it is. For example, assume that you have typed in “piano tuner” in the search engine. As a search result, ⓑ you see a video of an adorable cat playing the piano. Would you click on it? You would, along with many others, even though it has nothing to do with piano tuning. ⓒ The search engine then learns that the video is relevant to piano tuning and that it is okay to show a cat playing the piano when people are searching for piano tuners. This isn’t just true for search engines, but also on social media platforms, ⓓ which learn based on what you and others have clicked on before, not based on the accuracy of the information. In other words , the search engine learns that the link you previously clicked on is relevant to your search question, even though it is not. ⓔ When this irrelevant information, however, is clicked enough frequently, it can appear to be relevant and then mislead internet users.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ중 어법상 어색한 것은? (1점)
① ⓐ     ② ⓑ     ③ ⓒ     ④ ⓓ      ⑤ ⓔ
윗글에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? (0.7점)
① People tend to click on the most eye-catching link among the search results.
② Search engines learn information based on users’ clicking behavior.
③ Even irrelevant information can appear to be relevant if it is clicked frequently.
④ Search engines determine search results based on the accuracy of the information.
⑤ Social media platforms also learn based on users’ clicking data.

If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. This is an example of something known as (A)_____________ (B)_____________ ― when government support alters the decisions firms take. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. Although the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, encouraging risky and poor decision making.
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸(A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
Turing wanted to see if a machine could be as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a machine could imitate human behavior, why wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”

This question led Turing to design the “imitation game,” which also became known as the “Turing test.” The game itself was simple: A human participant would exchange a series of typed interactions with two respondents, a computer and a human being. After a set period of time, the participant would be asked to state which answers came from the computer and which came from the human being. If the participant failed to distinguish one from the other, the computer had passed the Turing test. It might be then inferred that the computer had the ability to think like a human.

Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually happen so consistently that machines would be considered intelligent. In the early days of computer science, he already imagined a world in which people could build machines that could “think.”
Machines may be considered int￼elligent when a human participant cannot ___(A)___ a computer’s responses from a human’s responses in a test designed to examine their ability to ___(B)___.
ㅣ 요  약  문 ㅣ
다음 글의 요지를 완성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 <보기>에서 골라 각 한 단어로 본문의 요지를 완성하시오. (단, 어형 변형 없음)

If you had wanted to create a “self-driving” car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, if o#nly means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.
Despite past limitations, advancements in (A)____________ now make it possible to (B)____________ the concepts￼ like self-driving cars and personalized medicine.
reach / attitude / remain￼ / enterprise /
condition / technology / avoid / increase

This is an example of something known as (A)_____________ (B)_____________ ― when government support alters the decisions firms take. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. 다음 글을 읽고, <요약문>의 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 서술하시오.

The arts and aesthetics offer emotional connection to the full range of human experience. “The arts can be more than just sugar on the tongue,” Anjan Chatterjee, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania, says, “In art, when there’s something challenging, which can also be uncomfortable, this discomfort, if we’re willing to engage with it, offers us the possibility of some change, some transformation. That can also be a powerful aesthetic experience.” The arts, in this way, become vehicles to contend with ideas and concepts that are difficult and uncomfortable otherwise. When Picasso painted his masterpiece Guernica in 1937, he captured the heartbreaking and cruel nature of war, and offered the world a way to consider the universal suffering caused by the Spanish Civil War. When Lorraine Hansberry wrote her play A Raisin in the Sun, she gave us a powerful story of people struggling with racism, discrimination, and the pursuit of the American dream while also offering a touching portrait of family life.
1. 주어진 단어들을 한 번씩만 사용하며 필요한 경우 변형하시오. 단, us는 두 번 사용하세요.￼
